$comment: W13.X4: answers for the OpenSSF Best Practices badge, Baseline series (OSPS Baseline, criteria v2025.10.10; follow v2026.02.19). Each criterion has a status (Met / Unmet / Unknown), a justification and the files that are its evidence; src/__tests__/ospsBaseline.test.ts fails when an evidence file is missing. The ids and titles were written offline from the OSPS Baseline as this lane knows it (baseline.openssf.org was not reachable): check them against the published list when registering (owner task W13.X3). `owner`: a repository setting only the owner can confirm. `gap`: a Level 2 gap, proposed as a task.

OSPS-AC-01.01.title: Multi-factor authentication for whoever can change the repository's settings
OSPS-AC-01.01.justification: A repository setting on GitHub, not a file: the owner confirms 2FA on the only admin account (owner task W13.X3).
OSPS-AC-01.01.owner: W13.X3: confirm 2FA on the admin account on bestpractices.dev

OSPS-AC-02.01.title: New collaborators get the lowest privileges by default
OSPS-AC-02.01.justification: A repository setting on GitHub: the owner confirms the default role for collaborators (owner task W13.X3). CODEOWNERS routes every review.

OSPS-AC-03.01.title: No direct commits to the primary branch
OSPS-AC-03.01.justification: Rulesets as code: main and verify/* need a pull request, status checks and signed commits; drift is checked by security:ruleset-drift.

OSPS-AC-03.02.title: The primary branch cannot be deleted
OSPS-AC-03.02.justification: The same rulesets carry a `deletion` rule for main and verify/*.

OSPS-BR-01.01.title: CI/CD input parameters are sanitized before use
OSPS-BR-01.01.justification: No GitHub Actions; the Buildkite pipeline and ci:local take no free-form parameters into shells; check-no-workflows keeps it so.

OSPS-BR-01.02.title: Branch names are sanitized before CI uses them
OSPS-BR-01.02.justification: ci:local and the PR gate read refs through git with argument arrays (no shell interpolation).

OSPS-BR-03.01.title: The project's official channels use encrypted transport
OSPS-BR-03.01.justification: The app is served over https only, with Strict-Transport-Security in public/_headers; headers --check keeps the security headers as declared.

OSPS-BR-03.02.title: Distribution channels use encrypted transport
OSPS-BR-03.02.justification: Releases, the plugin registry and the updater are https; downloads are verified (signature, provenance).

OSPS-BR-07.01.title: No unencrypted secrets in version control
OSPS-BR-07.01.justification: gitleaks with the project's config runs in ci:local and on every PR in Buildkite.

OSPS-DO-01.01.title: User guides for every basic function
OSPS-DO-01.01.justification: The documentation site, in English and Hebrew.

OSPS-DO-02.01.title: A guide to reporting defects
OSPS-DO-02.01.justification: COMMUNITY.md: bugs go to GitHub Discussions → Beta feedback (a form); accessibility has an issue form.

OSPS-GV-02.01.title: A public way to discuss changes and obstacles
OSPS-GV-02.01.justification: GitHub Discussions with forms, described in COMMUNITY.md (English and Hebrew).

OSPS-GV-03.01.title: The contribution process is documented
OSPS-GV-03.01.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md (English and Hebrew) and the contributor docs.

OSPS-LE-02.01.title: The source code is under an OSI-approved licence
OSPS-LE-02.01.justification: LICENSE at the root; the licence gate checks every dependency against licenses.allow.json.

OSPS-LE-02.02.title: Released software assets are under an OSI-approved licence
OSPS-LE-02.02.justification: Releases are built from this repository under LICENSE; THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md ships with them.

OSPS-LE-03.01.title: The licence is in the repository as LICENSE

OSPS-LE-03.02.title: The licence is shipped with released assets
OSPS-LE-03.02.justification: Gap: the release records the licence's SHA-256 (scripts/release.mjs) but no check shows LICENSE inside every release artefact.
OSPS-LE-03.02.gap: Ship LICENSE and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md in every release artefact, and make release-gate check it

OSPS-QA-01.01.title: The source code is publicly readable at a static URL

OSPS-QA-01.02.title: A public record of changes: who and when
OSPS-QA-01.02.justification: Git history on GitHub, plus CHANGELOG.md and the release notes.

OSPS-QA-02.01.title: Direct dependencies are listed in a standard file
OSPS-QA-02.01.justification: package.json and package-lock.json (and Cargo.toml for the desktop app); lockfile-check keeps the lockfiles clean (W13.X6).

OSPS-QA-04.01.title: Subprojects are listed
OSPS-QA-04.01.justification: README.en.md lists the sub-projects (the MCP server, the sync server) in its layout section.

OSPS-QA-05.01.title: No generated executables in version control
OSPS-QA-05.01.justification: The hygiene check and .gitignore keep build output out.

OSPS-QA-05.02.title: No unreviewable binary artefacts in version control
OSPS-QA-05.02.justification: THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md lists the bundled third-party assets; datasets are fetched, not committed (eval:public fails on a dataset file in the repo).

OSPS-AC-04.01.title: CI/CD tasks get the lowest permissions by default
OSPS-AC-04.01.justification: No GitHub Actions at all (check-no-workflows), so there is no workflow token to scope.

OSPS-BR-02.01.title: Each release has a unique version
OSPS-BR-02.01.justification: Semantic versions from the commits; each release is the git tag vX.Y.Z (scripts/release.mjs prepare --tag), and a tag name exists once.

OSPS-BR-04.01.title: Each release has a log of functional and security changes

OSPS-BR-05.01.title: Standard tooling installs the dependencies
OSPS-BR-05.01.justification: npm ci with a lockfile, ignore-scripts by default (W13.X6).

OSPS-BR-06.01.title: Releases are signed, or have a signed manifest of hashes
OSPS-BR-06.01.justification: Sigstore signatures and SLSA provenance for every release file; verify.mjs checks both.

OSPS-DO-06.01.title: How dependencies are chosen, obtained and tracked is documented
OSPS-DO-06.01.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md and the licence policy; renovate and dependabot configs; the install-script list (W13.X6).

OSPS-GV-01.01.title: A list of members with access to sensitive resources
OSPS-GV-01.01.justification: CODEOWNERS and security/reviewers.json; SECURITY.md lists the maintainers and their keys.

OSPS-GV-01.02.title: Roles and responsibilities are documented
OSPS-GV-01.02.justification: The second-maintainer and independent-review docs say who may do what.

OSPS-GV-03.02.title: Contribution requirements (style, tests, review) are documented
OSPS-GV-03.02.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md and the contributor checks docs.

OSPS-LE-01.01.title: Contributors assert they may contribute (DCO or CLA)
OSPS-LE-01.01.justification: Gap: no DCO or CLA is required today.
OSPS-LE-01.01.gap: Require a DCO sign-off (Signed-off-by) on every commit, checked by pr:check

OSPS-QA-03.01.title: Status checks must pass before merging
OSPS-QA-03.01.justification: Required status checks in the rulesets; pr:check is the gate (no Actions).

OSPS-QA-06.01.title: Automated tests run before merging
OSPS-QA-06.01.justification: Vitest, e2e and the gates in ci:local and Buildkite's pr-check job.

OSPS-SA-01.01.title: Design documentation of the system's actions and actors
OSPS-SA-01.01.justification: SECURITY.md, Security architecture: data at rest and in transit, the plugin sandbox, telemetry, authentication.

OSPS-SA-02.01.title: Documentation of external software interfaces
OSPS-SA-02.01.justification: The plugin documentation (and the plugin API report of W13.L1).

OSPS-SA-03.01.title: A security assessment of the likely and high-impact threats
OSPS-SA-03.01.justification: Threat cases and findings under security/ (attacks, findings.json, the crypto audit).

OSPS-VM-01.01.title: A coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy with response times
OSPS-VM-01.01.justification: SECURITY.md: CRA Article 14 timelines (24 h / 72 h / 14 days), safe harbour; security:page.

OSPS-VM-03.01.title: A private way to report vulnerabilities
OSPS-VM-03.01.justification: GitHub private vulnerability reporting must be turned on by the owner (the API call was refused to lanes, D1 16.11); until then security.txt points to a public issue.
OSPS-VM-03.01.owner: W13.X3/X2: turn on private vulnerability reporting

OSPS-VM-04.01.title: Vulnerability data is published (advisories, CVE via GHSA)
OSPS-VM-04.01.justification: SECURITY.md: advisories are GitHub Security Advisories with CVE ids; the hall of fame credits reporters.
